Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The current bug report describes an issue where `DateFormatUtils.format` does not correctly change the Calendar TimeZone in certain situations. The failing test `testFormat_CalendarIsoMsZulu` constructs a `Calendar` object in a way that causes `Calendar.setTimeZone` to not correctly change the Calendar's fields. This results in the test failing when comparing the formatted date with the expected value. 

Looking at the code snippet of the failing test `testLang538`, it constructs a `GregorianCalendar` object with GMT-8 timezone, sets the date and time, and then uses `FastDateFormat` to format the date. This scenario matches the issue reported, where the constructed Calendar object causes problems with changing TimeZones.

To locate the fault, we need to inspect the implementation of `DateFormatUtils.format` and how it handles changing Calendar TimeZones in certain situations.

I will now proceed to get the code snippet of the `DateFormatUtils.format` method to further analyze the root cause of the issue.

messages.name: get_code_snippet
messages.content: "197 :     public static String format(Calendar calendar, String pattern) {\n198 :         return format(calendar, pattern, null, null);\n199 :     }"

The `DateFormatUtils.format` method simply delegates the formatting to another method without directly handling the TimeZone changes. To resolve the issue, we need to ensure that the Calendar TimeZone changes are correctly handled within the `DateFormatUtils.format` method itself.

I will now suggest a method that needs to be fixed.
org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateFormatUtils.format(java.util.Calendar, java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
